item.text:
1. Lighthouses help ships identify coastlines and hazards.
2. A lighthouse usually pairs a tall structure with a light source.
3. Fresnel lenses use concentric rings to focus light into a beam.
4. Augustin-Jean Fresnel invented the modern lighthouse lens in the 19th century.
5. Lighthouse lights often flash in repeating patterns called characteristics.
6. Mariners can use a lighthouse’s flash pattern to identify it.
7. Fog signals help warn ships when fog hides a lighthouse’s light.
8. Some lighthouses use horns, bells, or sirens as fog signals.
9. Early lighthouses used open fires as beacons.
10. The Pharos of Alexandria was one of the ancient world’s most famous lighthouses.
11. The Pharos stood on the island of Pharos near Alexandria, Egypt.
12. The Tower of Hercules in Spain has served as a lighthouse since Roman times.
13. The Tower of Hercules is a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
14. Lighthouses have been built on shorelines, islands, reefs, and offshore platforms.
15. A lighthouse’s height affects how far its light can be seen over the horizon.
16. The elevation of a light also affects its visibility range.
17. Lighthouse keepers once maintained lamps, lenses, and mechanical equipment.
18. Many lighthouses were automated during the 20th century.
19. Some former lighthouse keeper residences are now museums or visitor centers.
20. Lighthouse colors and patterns can help distinguish one tower from another.
21. A lighthouse painted in horizontal bands is often called a daymark.
22. A lighthouse may have a different appearance by day than it does at night.
23. Some lighthouses are built on screw-pile foundations in shallow water.
24. The Bell Rock Lighthouse stands on a reef off Scotland’s east coast.
25. The Eddystone Lighthouse has been rebuilt several times because of storms and erosion.
26. Some lighthouses are constructed from stone to withstand severe weather.
27. Many coastal lighthouses have balconies around their lantern rooms.
28. The lantern room is the glass-enclosed space that houses the light apparatus.
29. A lighthouse’s gallery is the walkway around its lantern room.
30. Lighthouse lights can be white, red, or green depending on their purpose and location.
31. Sector lights show different colors across different directions.
32. Some navigational lights are mounted on towers that are not traditional lighthouse buildings.
33. Lightships once served as floating beacons where building a lighthouse was impractical.
34. Buoys can carry lights to mark channels and hazards.
35. Lighthouse beams can be visible from many miles away in clear conditions.
36. The range of a lighthouse is limited by weather and atmospheric conditions.
37. Salt spray can corrode lighthouse equipment and building materials.
38. Lighthouses are often placed near dangerous shoals or harbor entrances.
39. Lighthouse lenses may rotate to create a repeating flash.
40. Many lighthouses remain recognizable landmarks even after their lights are decommissioned.
